title: NATO-IP4 Relations Remain Stronger Than the Last Two Summits Suggest
gist: For the second straight year, the leaders of Australia, Japan, New Zealand and South Korea skipped the NATO summit, this time in Ankara in July 2026, but the author argues this reflects the design of the summits rather than any cooling of NATO-Indo-Pacific ties. She contends leader-level attendance is no longer the necessary driver of the relationship, which continues at working levels such as the NATO Military Committee chiefs-of-defense sessions.

insights.claim: The July 2026 NATO Summit in Ankara marked the second consecutive year that the leaders of the IP4 group — Australia, Japan, New Zealand and South Korea — did not attend.
insights.speaker: Mirna Galic
insights.so_what: Headline optics of Indo-Pacific disengagement from NATO are the surface story; check the working-level channels before repricing alliance-linked defense exposure.
insights.locator: A notable feature of the July 2026 NATO Summit in Ankara

insights.claim: The primary variable determining IP4 leader attendance at recent NATO summits was the nature and design of the summits themselves, not any decline in NATO or IP4 appetite for engagement.
insights.speaker: Mirna Galic
insights.so_what: Attribute attendance gaps to summit agenda-setting rather than strategic drift, and avoid extrapolating a NATO-Asia rupture from a guest list.
insights.quote: the main variable affecting the presence of the IP4 leaders was not the interest of NATO and IP4 countries in continued engagement, but the nature of the summits themselves

insights.claim: Interpreting the two-year absence of Indo-Pacific partner leaders as evidence that NATO-IP4 relations are deteriorating is a tempting but unsupported reading of the record.
insights.speaker: Mirna Galic
insights.so_what: A contrarian read against the consensus narrative of transatlantic-Indo-Pacific decoupling, relevant to positioning on European and Asian defense procurement linkages.
insights.quote: It may be tempting to see this as evidence that NATO-IP4 relations are on the downturn, but a deeper analysis does not support such a conclusion.

insights.claim: Regular leader-level attendance at annual NATO summits is no longer clearly a necessary driver of NATO-Indo-Pacific partner relations, implying the substance has migrated to other institutional channels.
insights.speaker: Mirna Galic
insights.so_what: Track defense-ministerial and military-committee level engagement as the real indicator of NATO-Asia cooperation depth rather than summit photo-ops.

insights.claim: The chiefs of defense of the United States, Australia, Japan, New Zealand and South Korea convened for a dedicated 'Partners in the Indo-Pacific' session at the 194th NATO Military Committee chiefs-of-defense meeting in Brussels in January 2026.
insights.speaker: Mirna Galic
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that military-to-military coordination continued through the leader-summit gap, supporting sustained interoperability and joint-standards work.

insights.claim: The strategic rationale for continued NATO-IP4 cooperation is as strong as ever given the current geopolitical climate, which argues for persistence of the relationship regardless of summit optics.
insights.speaker: Mirna Galic
insights.so_what: Underlying demand for cross-theater defense integration should keep supporting Indo-Pacific and European defense-industrial linkages even in years with weak diplomatic signaling.
insights.quote: The logic for continued cooperation between NATO and the IP4 is as strong as ever in the current geopolitical climate.
